absent: Complete field layout and sizing of keeper, read base and vdso shared structures beyond the fields observed in use.
Behavior of shadow commit, restore, coarse refresh, clock read and delta helpers not shown.
Rules for tai offset changes, leap second handling and frequency discipline beyond the call sites observed.
Semantics of vdso write markers and architecture synchronization hooks.
Lifecycle of timer objects including creation, deletion, signal delivery and cache management beyond identifier allocation.
Contents of realtime and monotonic clock operation tables and the global clock list.
Derivation of timer bucket count and mask and initialization of the global timer table.
Behavior of namespace time adjustments, high resolution sleep and wall time setting paths.
Exact auditing record contents and low level timer notification effects.
Conditions selecting no operation versus full readable publication builds and disabled auxiliary builds.

findings.text: Publishing of core keeper state to the shared readable time area is available to in-kernel callers, covering coarse and high resolution views together with timer resolution and architecture synchronization.
Publication of auxiliary keeper state to its dedicated readable slot is available, selecting the slot from keeper identity and honoring validity.
Publication of timezone offset fields to the shared readable area is available with architecture synchronization.
Boot time compensation for a local persistent clock is available, injecting a zone derived offset when configured.
Adjustment interface for frequency, offset and leap related controls is available, combining validation, auditing and change notification.
Readout of auxiliary clocks in both scalar and broken down forms is available, reporting failure when the clock is absent or invalid.
System calls for reading wall, monotonic and boot time and their resolutions are provided in both native and compat width variants, rejecting other identifiers.
System calls for sleeping until a relative or absolute deadline on wall, monotonic or boot clocks are provided in native and compat forms with restart handling.
System call for setting wall time from a compat width representation is provided, limited to the wall clock.
Timer hash buckets each pair mutual exclusion with a hash chain head for timers sharing that bucket.
Global timer table state groups the bucket array, its mask and the timer object cache with alignment and post init protection.
Clock configuration published for readable use carries last cycle count, mask, multiplier and shift, with an optional overflow bound when protected.
Monotonic base is derived from wall seconds plus the wall to monotonic offset expressed as a scalar time, while raw base is derived from raw seconds alone.
Whole second carry from combined fractional parts is folded into the seconds count before publication, keeping fractional parts canonical.
Conversion parameters for coupled clock events are refreshed only when coupling is enabled and supported and when multiplier or shift changed, using division to derive multiplier and bound.

Readable time publication shares a single clock mode across coarse and raw views and refreshes high resolution details only when the mode signals capability, while coarse views and resolution remain always refreshed.

Monotonic and boot readable timestamps combine wall seconds with monotonic offsets and shifted fractional parts normalized by whole second subtraction, with boot adding its dedicated offset and raw and tai exposing their own seconds with shared or raw fractions.

Auxiliary readable publication selects its slot from keeper identity, forces an unavailable mode when the keeper is invalid, and otherwise publishes configuration plus a normalized timestamp combining wall and auxiliary offsets.
Empty definitions of readable publication exist for builds without that support, providing no behavior.
Forwarding advances both monotonic and raw accumulators from the same cycle delta in bounded chunks limited by the clock maximum, normalizing after each chunk and refreshing coarse values at the end.
Normalization moves whole seconds from shifted fractional accumulators into their respective seconds counters independently for monotonic and raw.
Wall offset injection requires a canonical sub second part, forwards the shadow keeper first, and on validation failure restores the shadow without side effects.

Core injection validates the resulting wall time and preserves monotonicity by adjusting both wall and wall to monotonic parts oppositely, while auxiliary injection prevents negative results by checking the sum of current time and accumulated offset.
A keeper counts as core when auxiliary support is disabled or its identity matches the core identity.
Timezone publication copies minutes west and daylight fields to the shared area followed by architecture synchronization.
Minimal clock readout supports only wall, monotonic and boot identifiers, adding namespace adjustments for monotonic and boot, and rejects others.
Resolution queries report a single global high resolution timer granularity for supported clocks and reject others, with failure propagated on faulty user storage.

Sleep requests are accepted only for supported clocks with valid times, with absolute waits using namespace translated deadlines and no remainder and with restart state recording width appropriate remainder handling.
Compat width time interfaces mirror native behavior through older fixed width user representations for get, resolution, sleep and wall set.
Timer bucket selection hashes the owning signal identity together with the numeric identifier masked to table size.
Timer lookup by identifier requires both matching numeric identifier and matching owner, with a transient marker bit distinguishing fully initialized timers from reserving ones.

Timer identifier allocation guarantees uniqueness via explicit reservation reporting busy on collision with allocator advancement and via automatic search clamped to non negative range with rescheduling on contention reporting exhausted only after full scan.
Wall clock timer callbacks delegate reads to current wall readout and delegate set and adjust to the global wall set and adjust paths.

Global adjustment is accepted only after input validation with randomness mixing, with liveness required, and commits offset injection with unit conversion plus tai offset or leap maintenance plus immediate frequency advancement as requested.
Outer adjustment wrapper provides auditing of offset injection and discipline results with timer subsystem signaling on change and low level timer notification about second changes.
Auxiliary identity mapping translates between clock identifier and keeper index by fixed offset, with disabled builds always reporting absence.
Auxiliary readout combines stored base with auxiliary offset plus freshly computed sub second part, failing when data is missing or invalid.
Leap state refresh copies the shadow next leap value to the live keeper under protection.
Timer helper macros provide scoped acquisition with failure return and a scope alias, while unlock tolerates null timers.
Local persistent clock compensation derives a whole second adjustment from zone minutes and injects it once at boot.
Auxiliary offset update keeps scalar and broken down representations consistent.
Wall addition preserves canonical form with coarse refresh while incorporating seconds and shifted sub second parts.
Realtime and monotonic timer behaviors are provided through dedicated clock operation tables referenced from a global clock list.
Wall offset injection holds the core keeper lock with interrupts saved across the shadow update.
Global adjustment holds the keeper lock with interrupts saved across validation of liveness, offset handling and discipline updates.
Timer insertion holds the target bucket lock while checking duplicates and linking the new timer, preventing duplicate identifiers under race.
Timer lookup traverses hash chains under read side protection without bucket exclusion, relying on owner matching for safety.
Per timer exclusion is released with interrupt restoration and tolerates absent timers.
Auxiliary reads use sequence protection with retry on concurrent writer, while leap propagation uses write side sequence exclusion.
Readable time publication is bracketed by begin and end markers for the whole area or for a single auxiliary clock, with architecture hooks outside the critical section.
Shadow keeper edits transition through forwarded to modified to committed, with a restore transition to live on validation failure.
Timer identifiers transition among unallocated, reserved with transient invalid marker, and visible, with busy on explicit collision and exhausted on full table.
Readable clocks transition between unavailable and available modes based on keeper validity and underlying capability, with unavailable skipping high resolution refresh.
Unbounded cycle deltas are split to respect the clock maximum per step, avoiding multiplication overflow in fractional accumulation.
Negative resulting time and non canonical sub second inputs are rejected with restoration, preventing invalid wall or auxiliary states.
Reads during suspension or against invalid keepers are detected and reported as failure rather than returning stale values.
Duplicate timer identifiers under concurrent creation are prevented by rechecking under bucket exclusion.
User memory faults during time transfer are reported distinctly from invalid identifier or invalid value errors.
Timer creation accepts a sentinel requesting automatic identifier allocation whose value equals the most negative integer.
